meta.title: Populist attitudes
meta.question: Should the people or their representatives decide?
meta.measure: Average position on populist attitudes, from 0 (trust in elected representatives) to 10 (the people against the elite)
meta.anchor: Pooled from questions on whether the people or politicians should decide and on politicians' honesty and concern for ordinary people, with every answer placed on 0 to 10 and the trend read on the scale of an average question.

items.wording: Only when there's trouble are politicians interested in the views of the people (agree/disagree)
items.notes: Consolidation of Democracy in CEE, 1991 and 2000, 2 surveys.

items.wording: Parties only serve their leaders' interests (agree/disagree)
items.notes: Consolidation of Democracy in CEE, January 1991 and March 2000, 2 surveys.

items.wording: Ordinary people are always excluded from power (agree/disagree)
items.notes: Consolidation of Democracy in CEE, 1991 and 2000, 2 surveys.

items.wording: Politicians are glad if people don't interfere in their matters (agree/disagree)
items.notes: Consolidation of Democracy in CEE, 1991 and 2000, 2 surveys.

items.wording: Politicians do their best to seek the views of the people (agree/disagree; disagree = populist)
items.notes: Consolidation of Democracy in CEE, 1991 and 2000, 2 surveys.

items.wording: These days only those who want to make their fortune get involved in politics (agree/disagree)
items.notes: Consolidation of Democracy in CEE, 1991 and 2000, 2 surveys.

items.wording: Politicians care little about other people (agree-disagree)
items.notes: POLPAN 1993 and 1998, 2 waves; in 1993 about half the wave was not asked (code -10, questionnaire version).

items.wording: Most politicians, whatever they say, care only about their own careers (agree 10, disagree 0)
items.notes: CBOS's battery on the electorates' psychological characteristics: microdata 1995-2015, reports May-June 2019 and April-May 2023 (two surveys pooled each), which print only agree/disagree, so coded so in both.

items.wording: To hold any office in our country you cannot be an honest person (agree 10, disagree 0)
items.notes: CBOS's battery on the electorates' psychological characteristics: microdata 1995-2015, reports May-June 2019 and April-May 2023 (two surveys pooled each), which print only agree/disagree, so coded so in both.

items.wording: Those elected to parliament quickly lose touch with the people (agree-disagree)
Parties are only interested in people's votes, not in their opinions (agree-disagree)
items.notes: PGSW 1997.

items.wording: Being elected to parliament depends on connections, not knowledge and ability (agree-disagree)
items.notes: PGSW 2001 and 2005.

items.wording: Politicians care mainly about their own interests (agree-disagree)
items.notes: PGSW 2001 and 2005.

items.wording: Do you think that politicians in general care what people like you think? (hardly any ... most politicians care)
items.notes: European Social Survey round 1 (2002), 1 survey; the item of EES_POLITICIANS_CARE.

items.wording: Would you say that politicians are just interested in getting people's votes rather than in people's opinions? (nearly all just interested in votes ... nearly all interested in opinions)
items.notes: European Social Survey round 1 (2002), 1 survey; the item of PGSW_VOTES_ONLY.

items.wording: Among those who govern there are many corrupt people (agree-disagree)
items.notes: POLPAN 2008, 1 wave.

items.wording: Politicians do not care what people really think (agree-disagree)
items.notes: POLPAN 2008, 1 wave.

items.wording: Most elected officials care what people like me think (completely agree ... completely disagree)
items.notes: Pew Global Attitudes fall 2009 and spring 2019, 2 surveys with Polish answers (2012 has the question but not for Poland).

items.wording: Which comes closer to your view: most government officials care what people like me think, or most do not care? (volunteered neither/both at 5)
items.notes: Pew Global Attitudes spring 2014, 1 survey (the 2017 version was not asked in Poland).

items.wording: How much would you say that politicians care what people like you think? (0 not at all ... 10 completely)
items.notes: European Social Survey round 7 (2014), 1 survey.

items.wording: Improving people's living conditions is impossible because of irresponsible elites (1) vs possible regardless (5)
items.notes: PGSW 2015.

items.wording: Most politicians are decent and honest (1) vs all are corrupt and immoral (5)
items.notes: PGSW 2015.

items.wording: A democratic system where citizens, not elected officials, vote directly on major national issues to decide what becomes law: a very good ... very bad way of governing Poland?
items.notes: Pew Global Attitudes 2017, 2023 and 2024, 3 surveys. People versus representatives, as PGSW_POP_PEOPLE; drop if referendum-type items are to stay out (PGSW's demimp_referend and ESS votedir are not used).

items.wording: Does 'elected officials care what ordinary people think' describe Poland very well ... not well at all?
items.notes: Pew Global Attitudes spring 2018, 1 survey.

items.wording: Does 'most politicians are corrupt' describe Poland very well ... not well at all?
items.notes: Pew Global Attitudes spring 2018, 1 survey; the anti-elite pole of PGSW_POP_POLITICIANS.

items.wording: The people, and not politicians, should make our most important policy decisions (agree-disagree)
items.notes: European Election Study 2019 (online), 1 survey; the item of PGSW_POP_PEOPLE.

items.wording: What people call compromise in politics is really selling out one's principles (agree-disagree)
items.notes: PGSW 2019.

items.wording: Political elites are corrupt and interested in their own affairs (1-7)
items.notes: SWPS omnibus 2020 (SINGLE), 1 survey; random third (S1).

items.wording: Political decisions are right only when ordinary people, not those in power, take them (1-7)
items.notes: SWPS omnibus 2020 (SINGLE), 1 survey; random third (S1).

items.wording: Poland is divided into ordinary people and corrupt elites who exploit them (1-7)
items.notes: SWPS omnibus 2020 (SINGLE), 1 survey; random third (S1).

items.wording: The will of ordinary people should be the most important principle in this country's politics (1-7)
items.notes: SWPS omnibus 2020 on populism (SINGLE), 1 survey; a random third answered this generic version (S1); the S2 ('current government') and S3 ('whoever is in power') versions are left out.

items.wording: Politics is a fierce struggle between good, represented by ordinary people, and evil, which comes from the often corrupt elites (agree-disagree)
items.notes: SWPS COVID tracker wave 14 (July 2021), 1 survey; online. The middle code is 'hard to say' and is left out.

items.wording: The wisdom of the people, not the knowledge of experts, should guide those in power when they take important decisions (agree-disagree)
items.notes: SWPS COVID tracker wave 14 (July 2021), 1 survey; online. 'Hard to say' left out.

items.wording: How important for democracy is it that the will of the people cannot be stopped? (0-10)
items.notes: ESS round 10 (2021-22): self-completion by web and paper in Poland, where every other round was face to face, so a question of its own.

items.wording: Most politicians, whatever they say, care only about their own careers (agree 10, disagree 0)
items.notes: CBOS's mixed-mode surveys (CAPI, CATI or CAWI, the respondent's choice) from APiW 359 (May-June 2020), so a question of its own.

items.wording: To hold any office in our country you cannot be an honest person (agree 10, disagree 0)
items.notes: CBOS's mixed-mode surveys (CAPI, CATI or CAWI, the respondent's choice) from APiW 359 (May-June 2020), so a question of its own.

items.wording: Politicians take into consideration the concerns of citizens like me (agree-disagree)
items.notes: European Election Study 2024.

items.wording: The government is pretty much run by a few big interests looking out for themselves (agree-disagree, 1-7)
items.notes: FNW SWPS online survey, May 2025, 1 survey; random third (group 1; groups 2 and 3 say 'the current government' and 'governments are always').

items.wording: The government is mostly made up of crooks (agree-disagree, 1-7)
items.notes: FNW SWPS online survey, May 2025, 1 survey; random third (group 1).

items.wording: The will of the people should be the most important principle in this country's politics (agree-disagree, 1-7)
items.notes: FNW SWPS online survey, May 2025, 1 survey; asked of a random third (wording group 1; groups 2 and 3 say 'highest principle').

items.wording: The will of ordinary people should take precedence over decisions taken by judges and experts (agree-disagree)
items.notes: FNW SWPS online survey, December 2025, 1 survey. People against courts and experts: could also sit in Courts and the government.

items.wording: Laws should always be obeyed, even if they do not serve the will of the people (agree-disagree; disagree = populist)
items.notes: BDCS survey, Poland 2025 (SINGLE), 1 survey.
